authority: CLAUDE.md §12.3 (contradictions between tiers are resolved explicitly and recorded, never silently resolved by picking the convenient source), §9.4 (durable decisions are written down), §13.7 (no silent weakening of a check). Operator-directed ticket plans/fieldwise_tickets.md ticket 1, executing plans/fieldwise_reinstantiation_plan.md §6. NOT a constitutional amendment.
contradiction: The vault holds 140 nodes across 22 folders and describes the superseded project. Folder 11_objectives holds five objectives about probabilistic multi-sensor diagnosis of a latent field state. Folder 14_work_packages holds five work packages built on Route B and PlanetScope. Folder 16_risks holds ten risks, six of them about PlanetScope access, SAR retrieval and Route A cost. Folder 19_proposal_sections holds Part B sections written from that architecture. Tier 3 is being reseeded from the FIELDWISE draft, which replaces the methodological architecture itself and not only its wording. Vault and Tier 3 therefore assert different project facts.
decision: QUARANTINE NOW, RE-AUTHOR AFTER THE RUN. The vault is left byte-unchanged and is declared superseded by this record. Phases 1-8 run from the hand-lifted Tier 3 of tickets 3-5. The vault is re-authored against the resulting Tier 3 in ticket 12.
why_the_vault_does_not_block_the_run: The compiled manifest binds canonical_pack_deriver to runner/phase8_canonical_pack.py, which reads Tier 3 docs. The graph-sourced variant runner/graph_canonical_pack.py is bound to no node. Compilation from the graph is opt-in: `python -m runner --from-graph <config>` stages to docs/tier4_orchestration_state/graph_compile/staging/ and never writes canonical paths, and the cutover needs an explicit human `tools/promote_graph_staging.py --apply`. That is the dod-1d 'parallel + explicit promote' ruling. Nothing in the Phase 1-8 path reads the vault.
why_not_re_author_first: Re-authoring costs a full vault pass before anything runs, and it would author the graph against a Tier 3 that does not exist yet. Sequencing the vault after the run lets ticket 12 regenerate it from settled FIELDWISE Tier 3 records rather than from the draft twice.
accepted_consequence: runner/graph_claim_verifier.py audits Tier 5 claim ids against vault node ids. Once ticket 10 writes FIELDWISE Tier 5 sections, the verifier fails, because the claim ids will name FIELDWISE nodes the vault does not hold. That failure is honest and expected while this record is open. It is recorded here so a later reader does not mistake it for a regression, and it must not be silenced by relaxing the verifier.
current_state_note: tests/runner/test_graph_claim_verifier.py::test_real_vault_every_claim_traces and ::test_cli_real_vault_exit_0 were already failing before this purge, and they now fail for a second reason: the Tier 5 sections they read are deleted. Both are cleared by ticket 12, not by ticket 11.
what_stays: Folders 00_meta, 01_sources, 09_terminology, 90_dashboards and 99_governance are largely project-neutral and survive the re-authoring.
how_it_is_re_authored: tools/author_msca_proposal_graph.py is the deterministic authoring path. Ticket 12 rewrites that tool for FIELDWISE rather than hand-editing nodes, so the vault stays reproducible from a script under §9.5.
closed_by: plans/fieldwise_tickets.md ticket 12 ('Re-author the vault for FIELDWISE'). Closing requires graph_claim_verifier to pass against the committed FIELDWISE Tier 5 sections, at which point this record is updated to status 'closed' with the closing commit named.
companion_records: dod-1d-open-q4-parallel-explicit-promote_2026-07-28.json — the ruling that keeps --from-graph non-destructive, which is what makes quarantine safe.
effect: The tier contradiction is declared rather than ignored. The run proceeds from Tier 3, and the claim verifier's failure has a named cause and a named owner.
